SMTO-DB-0001 — SMTO's database feature is missing a part it needs

GUID: ee29a986-795a-4be6-b455-422d45f1b02f
Slug: database-dependency-unavailable
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • SMTO can't work with databases right now because a piece of software it needs isn't installed correctly on the computer running SMTO. Nothing was sent to your database.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who installed SMTO to run ./install.sh again from the same SMTO folder on the computer that runs SMTO. The installer puts back the missing database software without touching your conversations or settings.
  2. When no Tasks are running, have them restart SMTO with ./startup.sh or the installed app. SMTO only loads newly installed software when it starts.
  3. Ask SMTO a simple read-only question about your database, such as "List the tables in this database". A small read-only question confirms the database feature works without changing any data.

What success looks like

  • SMTO answers a read-only database question instead of showing this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't delete the data folder, Gateway pairings or saved connections to fix this; turning on a Skill's permission won't install the missing software either.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server cannot import the sqlglot SQL parser, so the database Skill is unavailable and SQL classification stops before anything is sent to the database.

What this means

  • Database availability cannot import sqlglot, or the parser loader catches ModuleNotFoundError before SQL classification. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • Database availability cannot import sqlglot, or the parser loader catches ModuleNotFoundError before SQL classification.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the named missing module and which runtime loads the database parser before repairing an installation.

How to fix it

  • The server's Python environment cannot import sqlglot (pyproject.toml declares sqlglot>=26.0,<27.0). Rerun ./install.sh from the matching checkout as the account that runs the server, confirm import sqlglot succeeds in that environment, then restart the server once active work has settled. Do not delete saved state, Gateway pairing, credentials or browser profiles; granting a Skill permission does not install dependencies.
  • The smTO runtime is missing a required library or has an incompatible dependency. Rerun ./install.sh on the server from the matching checkout and restart it after installation succeeds. If the diagnostic identifies a Gateway-side client instead, repair that selected Gateway with its platform installer, then refresh metadata.
  • From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • Restart the repaired server after installation succeeds and active work is settled. If a Gateway environment was repaired, restart that Gateway, refresh its metadata and start a new task. Reconcile any uncertain operations before repeating them.
  • Confirm the named dependency loads in the failing server or Gateway environment and its installer audit passes before retrying.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm the named dependency loads in the failing server or Gateway environment and its installer audit passes before retrying. Reconcile any uncertain operations before repeating them.

How to verify the fix

  • Database availability and one supported read validate with the installed parser.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
